reasons: The excerpt explicitly recommends Okendo for surveys, identifies it as particularly for Shopify stores, and says it can be installed to collect unlimited responses depending on order data.
The cost concern for Hotjar surveys and feedback is stated in the excerpt and is a supported reason to consider the alternative.
The excerpt says the speaker often uses UserBrain instead of Hotjar and describes setting up remote testing with first-impression, cart/checkout, and B2B form-finding tasks.
The candidate preserves uncertainty in the price transcription and does not claim that UserBrain is functionally identical to Hotjar interviews.
The action is supported: the excerpt says custom funnels can be set up in Google Analytics 4 through the Explore tab and used to see progression through a site.

The trigger incorrectly requires a B2B homepage-to-contact-form-to-thank-you-page funnel. The excerpt presents that only as an example of a possible funnel, not as a condition for using GA4 custom funnels. Revise the trigger so wanting to analyze a custom site-navigation funnel is sufficient.

The claim accurately preserves the excerpt's conditional recommendation: when separate tools such as Okendo and UserBrain are acceptable, the speaker says there is no real downside and calls Clarity the best bet.
The candidate appropriately labels unaddressed integration and workflow overhead as unknown rather than asserting it away.
The excerpt states that Hotjar has different pricing tiers depending on traffic, gives the cited Plus-plan price and daily-session quantity, and says higher levels can become expensive.
The candidate does not invent details for the unspecified higher tiers and correctly notes that recency is not established by the excerpt.
The excerpt directly describes heatmap data as showing how far users scroll and where they click.
The action does not add unsupported benchmarks, interpretation thresholds, or platform-specific behavior beyond that description.

The excerpt supports the described client example: a lower-page shop-by-industry section had substantial clicks despite limited reach, and the speaker moved the same icons to the top of the homepage in an A/B test.

The completion item improperly turns a reported result from one client test into a completion criterion. The excerpt reports an ambiguous “18% ... in conversions” outcome; it does not say that an 18% conversion result is required to complete or validate this action. Move it to case-specific evidence or an unknown, and retain the missing unit/meaning of the reported conversion figure as unresolved.

The conditional action should be framed as a case-derived testing idea rather than a generally established rule, since the excerpt supplies one example and no broader decision rule, sample requirement, or test-validity criteria.

omissions.description: The excerpt also says that Clarity area maps can be examined at a more granular element level; this is distinct from inspecting overall click percentages or using them to select an A/B test.
omissions.quote: you can dig a lot deeper too and kind of dissect specific ele ments within the area map too

omissions.description: The excerpt directly identifies watching recordings of users on the website as a core behavior-analysis activity. The retained material discusses recording capability and platform selection, but does not represent this operational activity as its own advice.
omissions.quote: you can actually watch recordings of users on your website

source_limitations: The source is an informal, apparently automated transcript with ambiguous or corrupted terms, including “4 Z,” “contract form,” and an incomplete “18% uh in conversions” statement.

The source does not identify the recording date. Statements about pricing, free access, data limits, and product features may be time-bound; only Clarity's no-cost/no-data-limit statement is explicitly qualified as being at the time of recording.

Several recommendations rest on the speaker's preference or a single client anecdote, without test duration, sample size, baseline, statistical methodology, implementation details, or independent comparison data.
